tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local fixture continuing c23. Operation O5 and payload digest D5 remain unchanged. An old provider proof P_I5 is immutably bound to idempotency identity I5, covers complete I5 attempt history, is permanently sealed/quiescent for I5, and explicitly attests no irreversible effect for every I5 attempt. A later authoritative repository claim uses the same O5,D5 but rotates provider idempotency identity to I6. Test only whether P_I5 can support terminal negative closure for the I6 claim without a new provider proof or an independent provider-domain equivalence attestation. No concrete provider, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler state, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is tested.

premises: P_I5 is exact-bound only to O5,D5,I5.
P_I5 proves complete history, permanent sealing/quiescence, and explicit no-effect only for I5.
The later repository claim is authoritative but uses I6, a distinct provider idempotency identity.
No independent attestation proves that I6 aliases I5, shares the same provider attempt namespace, or is unable to create a new provider execution domain.
fixture.candidate_action: Reuse P_I5 to record terminal negative closure for the later O5,D5,I6 claim.
fixture.reason: The idempotency identity is part of the provider proof domain. P_I5 establishes absence of irreversible effect and permanent terminality only for I5. Rotating to I6 may create a distinct provider attempt namespace even when O5 and D5 are unchanged, so P_I5 contains no evidence about I6 attempts. Repository-claim freshness cannot expand the provider proof's identity scope. Therefore the old proof cannot justify negative closure for I6 unless an independent provider-domain equivalence/sealing attestation explicitly covers both identities.

weak_rule_falsified.rule: If logical operation and payload digest are unchanged, a complete sealed no-effect proof for one provider idempotency identity may be reused after rotation to another idempotency identity.
weak_rule_falsified.falsification: A distinct idempotency identity can denote a distinct provider execution namespace. Exact O5,D5 equality does not make an I5-scoped proof evidence about I6.

minimum_safe_conditions: Use a terminal proof exact-bound to the current idempotency identity I6; or

obtain an independent provider attestation that I5 and I6 are the same execution/proof domain, that no new attempts can exist under I6 outside the P_I5 history, and that permanent sealing/no-effect coverage explicitly extends across both identities.
Repository finalization must still use the current authoritative claim/fence with CAS and exact readback.

observations: Repository claim continuity in O5,D5 does not imply provider proof-domain continuity when the idempotency identity changes.
Permanent sealing is only as broad as the identity domain named by the proof unless explicit cross-identity equivalence evidence exists.
Cross-identity proof replay is therefore unsafe by default, while same-identity cross-claim replay from c23 can be safe under strict permanent-sealing premises.
inference: The safe replay boundary is identity-domain continuity, not merely operation/payload continuity. A terminal no-effect proof may survive repository claim-epoch changes when its exact provider identity is unchanged and permanently sealed, but it must not be projected across an idempotency-identity rotation without explicit provider-domain equivalence evidence.
